SEND Local Offer
The special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) Local Offer are excited to announce a series of ‘Local Offer Discovery Day’ events, which will take the online Local Offer onto the road and into YOUR community. These events will give families, young people and professionals the opportunity to learn more about the support available for children and young people with SEND. This is the first time we have run events of this kind, and we are asking for your support to help raise awareness amongst families who will benefit most. Please note, the events are open to ALL families and professionals.
Over the coming days, you will receive printed ‘Local Offer Discovery Days’ leaflets for all children in your school who are on SEN Support or who have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP).
Click here for more information.

Careers
Hampshire Futures provide independent careers advice, information and support with college applications, as well as information about technical education qualifications and apprenticeships to our young people.
We are developing our database of workplaces and links to local providers including those which we use for work experience. We strive to provide work place visits from year 7-11, as well as have visitors to the school to discuss their careers. This forms a part of the PSHE curriculum.
Opportunities for voluntary work experience in a range of sections through the Personal Development Programme (PDP) where students work towards ASDAN Accreditation. This area of study includes experience of interviews, application forms and CVs.
We have developed links with Enterprise Coordinators and they provide information to our students, parents and carers through information sharing.
Careers education is planned for across all subjects and referred to within lessons as well as access to displays linked to subject areas in all subject classrooms to ensure our young people have as much exposure to the opportunities available to them as possible.
The school uses The Gatsby Benchmarks to assess suitability, quality and areas for development in the school’s careers offer.
Detailed information on the careers opportunities and experiences we offer and are developing can be found in the Careers Policy.
Click here to view/download the detailed Careers programme of study.
Further advice and information regarding careers can be found on the National Careers Service website using the following link nationalcareersservice.direct.gov.uk.

The Communication and Interaction Team, now known as the Education and Inclusion Therapy Service, have been supporting Special Schools at a whole school and class level. For the time being, the Local Authority has made the decision to prioritise speech & language therapy for those children in special schools, who have this provision specified in their EHCP. FREE Support for Families
Barnardos – Hampshire Healthy Steps has been commissioned by Public Health to deliver a free offer for families with children aged 2 to 12 in Hampshire who would benefit from practical help to improve their families health and wellbeing.
The session is delivered across six fun interactive group sessions covering; healthy eating, sleep, oral health and physical activity.
Why is it important?
Unfortunately, we know that poor nutrition in early childhood has lifelong consequences – children are more likely to face malnutrition, obesity, tooth decay and poorer physical and mental health as they grow.​
20.7% of reception-aged children and 32.2% of Year 6 children in Hampshire are overweight or obese – prevalence in Year 6 ranges from 25.9% in Winchester to 39.5% in Gosport.
Three in ten children aged 5 to 19 years in Hampshire are ‘less active’, participating in under 30 minutes of exercise a day.
Around 14% of 5-year-olds in Hampshire have one or more decayed, missing, or filled teeth, ranging from 9.3% in Hart to 18% in the New Forest.
By working directly with families to understand barriers and set realistic goals, we can support healthier development and reduce the risks linked to poor nutrition, sleep and oral health.

Our Curriculum
A full range of curriculum subjects are taught throughout key stage 3 and 4, more detailed information regarding the curriculum coverage for individual subjects can be found on the curriculum tab of the website.
Learning Pathways
Every subject has a ‘Learning Pathway’ attached to it that enables students, staff, parents and carers to see the learning steps that are required and the pathways for each individual. The Learning Pathways map out the learning journey of each individual student with ambitious targets set for each individual. The Learning Pathways map the journey of a young person and enable all to see what next step the young person is required to make along their journey. The Learning Pathways have been developed by individual subject leaders and enable them to ensure knowledge and skills are embedded and that subject curriculum’s and cross-curricular planning is sequenced to develop those new knowledge and skills build upon what has come before in their learning journey.
Personal Development
Our curriculum aims to give our students access to a range of subjects and disciplines enabling them to become well-rounded British Citizens. Our ambition is for all our students to successfully and confidently contribute to society as they transition into adulthood. Students are fully supported over time in identifying their hopes and dreams for the future and we aim for them to leave the school with realistic aspirations that they are prepared and supported to achieve. Throughout their time at the school students experience and discuss the purpose of what they are learning in the context of everyday living and the world of work. The school utilises Play Therapy, ELSA, TALA, Thrive and CBT to support our young people in making progress with their personal development, mental health and wellbeing needs; access to these provisions is determined by the Wellbeing Team using our school database and Learning Pathways to target those young people that require the support and through a referral system that is discussed at weekly team meetings.
Social Skills, Life Skills and British Values
We always intend to give students the skills, knowledge and confidence for independent living and these are carefully planned into opportunities across all curriculum subjects as well as through the CoPE curriculum and Asdan Awards, where the students gain credits for accreditation in this area of the curriculum. Life skills, Social Skills and British Values are covered throughout the curriculum and carefully planned into schemes of work across all subjects. Thrive is delivered to students on a need basis that is determined by the school, ‘Thrive’ enables our young people to grown in confidence, independence and socially and enables individuals to develop the life skills they require to improve their communication and resilience.
Literacy and Numeracy
A wide range of subjects are delivered with functional Mathematics and English opportunities covered throughout individual subjects. Literacy and numeracy form a strong base of our curriculum and students access ‘Key Skills’ teaching in these subjects on a daily basis providing an opportunity to overlearn and practice these fundamental skills; this includes phonics teaching, guided reading and the opportunity to practice basic maths skills at a level appropriate to the young person.
Communication
Opportunities to improve communication is planned across the curriculum to enhance students’ ability to access the curriculum and to become functional communicators. Speech and Language Blank Level Scores are tracked throughout a young person’s time in the school to ensure that all classroom staff can support our young people in making improvements in this area of the curriculum. Due to the communication difficulties our young people present we do not deliver discrete modern foreign language (MFL) sessions but rather include them in our teaching of Spiritual, Moral, Social and Culture (SMSC) teaching. We do this to enable our young people to communicate efficiently in the English Language primarily, an area for which our students are often significantly delayed. Students identified as requiring more extensive work on their communication will access the Speech and Language Therapist (SALT) and the school’s two own Speech and Language Therapy Assistants (SALTA) and bespoke packages put into place to support progress in this area that is fundamental to accessing the wider curriculum more fully and successfully. Both SALTA work within a classroom setting, one English and the other always within a practical setting to enable them to work with individuals on specific language development. Some subject areas, such as PSHE focus on communication to track progress within The Learning Pathways enabling the teacher to specifically work on this aim within the lesson.
Personalised Provision
The school seeks and utilises the strengths of the individual students and will always personalise provision for those students with special talents and interests where this is appropriate for the student. We work in partnership with other settings, including local mainstream schools and colleges to provide this provision if we are not equipped for the delivery of a specific area. Appropriate support, monitoring and safeguarding checks are carried out prior and during a student accessing such a provision.
Learning outside the classroom
At Mark Way School we believe that students are inspired, motivated and learn a great deal from meaningful experiences outside the classroom. We aim to create as many learning experiences outside the classroom as possible, this includes exploring potential career paths and these being discussed throughout individual learning opportunities within subjects. In doing this we hope to promote a greater understanding of our local community, the skills required to live successfully and the opportunity to experience them within the safety net of the school context. Additionally, we hope to engender our students with the virtues that we feel are important for success in life. We believe that by experiencing more of their immediate outdoor environment they will leave us with a greater sense of British Values and their place within British Community.

Curriculum Impact
Our young people leave the school empowered with realistic aspirations to achieve even more and to contribute to society confidently and independently.
Students have a good understanding of the virtues required to function successfully in society and to gain the best possible life chances.
Students leave the school prepared for the next stage of their education or work equipped with outcomes that match and often exceed expectations given their starting points.
The impact of English can be seen in all lessons, where the pupils are expected to be able to communicate ideas clearly to others. This has built on and developed their own confidence in communicating their own thoughts and feelings on a variety of concepts. We work hard to give every pupil the opportunity to achieve the best that they can in English, with the aim that they go on to achieve a qualification that would support them in their future.
The impact of Maths can be seen across the curriculum by helping pupils think systematically to complete tasks or in the development of numeracy skills. The development of pupils learning journeys regardless of starting point and tracking development from there is vital. We strive to enable our learners to achieve their aspirational outcomes. The best advantage we can give our pupils is in their achievement of Entry level and GCSE qualifications.
The Key Skills curriculum carried out 4 days per week enables students to develop basic reading, writing and maths skills required for everyday life. Student reading, spelling show dramatic improvements because of the opportunity for very regular practice within the subject areas. Enabling students to access all areas of the curriculum.
Pupils will have a wider understanding of how the world around them works and they will be able to apply their knowledge and understanding of the areas of Biology, Chemistry and Physics along with their scientific enquiry skills in order to understand the impact of scientific processes on the world and themselves.
In the case of self-isolation, pupils will have access to the Science curriculum through the use of Microsoft teams and will be offered the same opportunities as pupils attending school. The use of video calls with the science teacher, educational videos, presentations, worksheets and open-ended tasks will be used to develop pupil’s knowledge of Science and ensure suitable progress is maintained. This will ensure that pupils are still provided with the same opportunities to develop their understanding in all areas of science.Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Education (SMSC).
Students will have accurate and relevant knowledge of SMSC. They will become individuals who are willing to share and reflect upon their own and others’ faiths, be able to work with others, regardless of gender, race or sexuality, understand changes and be eager for challenge.
The impact of Art education at The Mark Way School will be that students appreciate the importance of visual communication and how creativity is used in all cultures and societies to understand and connect people. Students will show ability in thinking creatively and have the knowledge that art can be used as platform for self-expression as a creative outlet. Students can access a GCSE qualification.
Design & Technology is deeply rooted in the STEM approach and as a result has cross-curricular ties with Math’s, Science, ICT and Art.

A lot of the core skills and problem solving serve as a basis for many life skills in and out of school allowing pupils to become more resourceful, innovative, enterprising and capable. They learn to develop a critical understanding of the impact of design and technology on daily life and the wider world.
Food and Nutrition allows all pupils to learn and develop transferable life skills that are suitable for use in and out of school. It ensures that pupils increase their cooking skills and built up a good knowledge of the Science that goes into cooking.
Students learn to cook a variety of predominantly savoury dishes and develop a repertoire of food that they can prepare and cook confidently and competently on their own. Accreditations at GCSE level will enable pupils to access future pathways in the Food Preparation / industry.

The adaption of the curriculum for students with SLD needs allows a continuation and development of core skills which are imperative for those students.
